title: Contingency Placement Agreements — Returned-Payment Reserve on the Trust Balance at Closing Settlement
content:
When fees owed on an agreement under the Contingency Placement Agreements are settled at closing, a reserve covering consumer payments that may still come back is held back from the trust balance held. The reserve is deducted from the trust balance held in arriving at the available trust balance, which is never less than zero.

## Reserve schedule

| Collections reversed as returned payments on the agreement in the 6 months before the payment | Reserve |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | all of the collections booked in the month before the payment (share 1) |
| 1 or 2 | half of those collections (share 0.5) |
| none | nothing |

As a clause: the reserve is all of the collections booked in the month before the payment where 3 or more collections were reversed as returned payments in the 6 months before the payment, half of those collections where 1 or 2 were so reversed, and nothing where none was.

## Notes

1. *Windows.* A window of a number of months before a date covers the dates after the same day that number of months earlier, up to and including that date. The month before the payment and the 6 months before the payment are both windows ending on the day of the payment.
2. *What counts.* Collections are the consumer payments booked to the agreement's trust balance. Only reversals for returned payments are counted; a reversal for an overpayment refund is not.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

Payment made on 2026-08-20. Collections booked from 2026-07-21 through 2026-08-20 total 1840.00 USD; a collection booked on 2026-07-20 falls outside the month.

| Returned-payment reversals dated after 2026-02-20 up to 2026-08-20 | Reserve |
|---|---|
| 4 | 1840.00 USD |
| 2 | 920.00 USD |
| 0 | nothing |

With a trust balance held of 1500.00 USD and a reserve of 1840.00 USD, and nothing else held back, the available trust balance is zero, not a negative figure.
